tagline.text: A hot spring resort with a Korean restaurant, in the Pansol spa district at the foot of Mount Makiling

location.label: Location
location.text: National Highway, Bagong Kalsada (Pansol area), Calamba, Laguna

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,300–10,000 (per person for a day pass, or per room for 1 night)

children.text: 88 Hotspring Resort sits in the middle of Calamba's Pansol hot spring district, on about 7 hectares at the foot of Mount Makiling, with around 9 natural hot spring pools. It is 1.5–2 hours from Manila by car, so it works equally well as a day soak or a 1-night getaway, and its Korean restaurant and massage center make it especially easy for Korean travelers.
Calamba is a city in Laguna about
50 km

south of Manila. Hot spring resorts cluster on the northern slopes of Mount Makiling, which has earned it the nickname "Spring Resort Capital of the Philippines." The resorts are concentrated in barangays such as Pansol, Bucal, Bagong Kalsada and Lingga, near the boundary with Los Baños. 88 Hotspring Resort is on the National Highway in Bagong Kalsada, a landmark at the end of the Pansol stretch.

According to the resort and several guides, the grounds cover about 7 hectares, and the pools are fed by odorless, clear bicarbonate mineral water that rises at the foot of Mount Makiling. There are 9 pools (some sources count 10 or 11), and the two hottest, the octagonal feng shui pools, reach up to
. The kids' pool is much cooler, and there are also a 5-foot-deep pool for swimming and quieter pools on the upper level, so you can choose to suit your taste.

Beyond the pools, the gardens have a lily pond, a small waterfall, a vegetable farm and a wishing well, and the resort has a Korean restaurant, a Filipino grill restaurant, a massage and spa center, a volleyball court, a firing range and a bar. It is said to have been operating since 2006, and its roughly 48 rooms come in seven types: Standard, Bamboo Deluxe, Bamboo Suite, Villa, Pension House, Executive and Nipa Hut.

This is less a flashy new resort than a long-established, mid-range hot spring complex, and some parts show their age. Even so, its closeness to Manila, reasonable prices and Korean menu are why Korean families and groups of friends keep coming back. It does not have a rustic, traditional feel, so if you are hoping for a hidden-forest atmosphere, Hidden Valley Springs, also in Laguna, is a better fit.
These are the hottest pools in the resort, with water reaching up to
. One is next to the kids' pool and the other beside the pension houses, and many people soak here on cool evenings or early mornings.

This pool, about 1.5 m deep, is beside the second level where the Korean restaurant is, and it is good for swimming or walking in the water. A videoke machine sits next to the largest pool, so it gets lively when groups gather.
It is much cooler than the adult pools and has two small slides and a shower fountain. Adults can sit in the nearby cottages and keep an eye on the children, so families head here first.

A few more steps up from the 5-foot pool, quieter pools with fewer people continue. Some reviews, however, say they are less well maintained than the lower pools, so take a look and decide for yourself.
A full-body massage was listed at about
, and a Korean-style package with sauna, body scrub and a facial massage costs about
extra (2017 and 2022 listings; some recent reviews report higher prices, so confirm on site). Bookings open at 7 a.m. and the last slot is around 7:30 p.m., so book as soon as you arrive.

There is a Korean restaurant on the second level near check-in, plus a Filipino grill restaurant called Makiling Inihaw Garden. It is an easy hot spring to find food that suits Korean tastes, whether you crave a hot soup or grilled pork belly.

The gardens, with a lily pond, an artificial waterfall, a wishing well and a vegetable farm, are good for a light walk between swims. There is said to be a forest trail too, but you will need to check its condition yourself.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: Leave in the morning, return in the evening

children.text: Drive from Manila (Makati or Ortigas) down SLEX and exit at Calamba. On weekends, leaving early means lighter traffic.
Check in, pay your entrance and check the lockers and showers. If you can, claim a cottage or a lounge chair first.
Start in the cooler pools to let your body adjust, then warm up in the octagonal feng shui pools in
10–15-minute
rounds. Do not stay in the hot water too long, and bring cold water.
Have lunch at the Korean restaurant or the Filipino grill. Ask at the entrance whether your day pass includes a meal credit.
If you booked the spa, this is the time for your massage. If not, stroll around the pond and gardens or play with the kids in the kids' pool.
When the sun lowers and it cools off, soak in the hot pools again, shower and head back to Manila. Northbound SLEX is very congested on Sunday evenings, so it is best to leave early.
Day entrance is generally listed as running from about 8 a.m. to 9–10 p.m. Call ahead to confirm road conditions and operating hours before you go.

items.title: 1-night stay
items.subtitle: Use both the evening hot pools and the morning pools

children.text: Arrive at check-in time, drop your bags and confirm that the room includes entrance for 2 people.
In the afternoon, when it is still quiet, start with the cooler pools and tour the pools one by one.
Have dinner at the Korean restaurant, and once you have digested, soak in the heated water of the night pools. Some pools close at midnight.
Reviews say the upper pools stay open late, so confirm the hours at the front desk before you go up.
Breakfast is often included in the room rate and is served as a simple plate at the Korean restaurant. Afterwards, take an easy walk through the gardens.
Pack up in time for check-out (around 11:30–12:00), and on the way back it is a good idea to stop at the Rizal Shrine in downtown Calamba.
Rooms usually include entrance and breakfast for 2 people. Extra guests have been listed at about
each, so make sure the headcount matches when you book.

items.title: From Manila by car or taxi

children.text: From Makati or Ortigas, take SLEX to the Calamba exit, go down the road, and turn right near SM Calamba, cross the railway and continue onto the National Highway. Search for "88 Hotspring Resort" in your map app.
With light traffic it takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
, and on weekends and Friday evenings it can take
2–3 hours
The resort has free parking on site, so driving yourself is the easiest option. Traffic around Pansol can back up even on weekdays.
Near Buendia on Taft Avenue, take a Greenstar Express bus bound for Santa Cruz or Calamba, which takes about
2–2.5 hours
. Tell the conductor to drop you near "Pansol" or the "88 Resort."
HM Bus Liner buses to Santa Cruz also leave from the Cubao EDSA terminal, and the trip is listed at about
3 hours
After getting off the bus, take a tricycle to the resort. Bus routes and terminals change often, so check before you leave.
Public transport information comes mostly from older reviews, so there are no exact timetables. If you have luggage or a group, renting a car or hailing a ride-hailing car such as Grab is better.
From Calamba Crossing, take a jeepney heading south along the Maharlika Highway toward Pansol and Bucal.
Tricycles go everywhere in Pansol. The regular fare is about
per km and a solo (special) ride is about
or so (a 2015 blog said ₱50), and the fare to the resort gate may differ, so ask the driver for the fare before you negotiate.

Hot springs are more enjoyable when it is cool. Calamba's dry season is short, January to April, and November–February is relatively cool, which makes it the best time to soak in water above 40℃. In March–May it is hot, so spend midday in the cooler pools and use the hot pools around dusk.

In the June–October rainy season, afternoon showers are frequent, and July–October gets the most rain. Soaking in the rain has its charm, but garden paths can be slippery. Weekends, public holidays, Holy Week and school vacations are crowded, with busy pools and possible waits, so aim for a weekday if you can.

Rooms are divided into Standard, Bamboo Deluxe and Suite, Pension House, Villa, Executive and Nipa Hut. The pension houses near the lake, gardens and waterfall are the quietest, while the villa rooms facing the kids' pool are convenient but noisy, it is said. The Executive rooms are on the second floor, so you have to climb stairs. Every room has air conditioning and a TV, but some reviews mention showers with only hot water or a sewer smell from the drains, so if you are sensitive, look at the room first.

For meals, there is the Korean restaurant on the second level near check-in (Korean dishes such as bulgogi, and reviews also mention grilled pork belly) and the Filipino grill restaurant, plus a snack bar between the pools. The food is mostly Korean and easy on Korean tastes, but remember that resort prices apply. Downtown Calamba and the Pansol area also have many Filipino home-cooking restaurants and barbecue places, so if you stay overnight it is worth going out for dinner once. If you plan to bring lots of food and cook outside, check the corkage policy in advance.
When you enter, be sure to ask exactly what the day pass covers, including locker, cottage, pool use and meal credit. The package varies by season.
Weekday mornings are the quietest. On weekends, go early and claim a cottage spot first.
Do not stay in the hot pools longer than
10–15 minutes
at a time, bring cold water and drink often. After leaving a hot pool, cool off in a cooler one.
Some reviews say certain shower rooms have no hot water or curtains that do not close properly. Bring flip-flops, a towel and a change of clothes.
The walkways are uneven, so avoid large suitcases, and bring insect repellent because of the mosquitoes.
The spa takes bookings from 7 a.m. Popular time slots fill up early, so book as soon as you arrive.
For an overnight stay, ask when you book whether the rate includes entrance for 2 people and breakfast. Also check the extra-guest rate in advance.
There are very many resorts with similar names in Pansol. Check the address "9061 National Highway, Bagong Kalsada" in your map app.
The road from Manila to Pansol is very congested on weekend and holiday evenings. If you leave late on a Sunday afternoon, getting back to Manila can take over 3 hours, so leave early.
Some pools are hotter than 40℃. People with heart or blood pressure problems, pregnant women and small children should avoid the hot pools, and do not get in after drinking alcohol.

Some reviews describe the place as having an adult-oriented atmosphere, or say the upper pools are less well maintained than the lower ones. If you bring children, check the kids' pool and the room location.
Prices, operating hours and pool counts differ between sources and change often. Before you go, confirm the latest information through the resort's official channels (phone or social media account).
The areas around the pools and the stairs are wet and slippery. Wear non-slip shoes rather than flip-flops.
Put valuables in a locker and carry only the minimum cash and cards. Prices inside are on the high side, so it is a good idea to prepare snacks in advance.
The mountain right behind the resort.
Mount Makiling & Los Baños
has tropical forest trails and a spa district, so it pairs well with the hot springs as a full-day trip.
